Individual advisory experience Advisory work by Shyam Sundar Pani and Makarand Datar as individuals, not work carried out by SetuHashi.

Developing two routes into Turkey

Using business relationships to develop market-entry opportunities—and recognising when conditions require a pause.

The objective

Help a consulting and technology business develop an entry into Turkey through a prospective client engagement and a local business partnership.

Shyam and Mak’s contribution

Drawing on Shyam’s network, the team connected with two chief executives and developed two potential routes into the market.

One involved a consulting and transformation engagement with an industrial minerals producer. The other involved a joint-venture strategy with a data services company.

Shyam and Mak worked with the business to develop these opportunities beyond initial introductions, connecting prospective relationships with engagement and partnership strategies.

The output

Two developed market-entry opportunities: a proposed consulting and transformation engagement, and a joint-venture strategy.

Status

Both advanced towards potential agreement but did not close. According to the contributors, shipping-cost pressures and currency and inflation uncertainty affected the conditions for proceeding. Both opportunities remain on hold.

Source: Shyam Sundar Pani and Makarand Datar’s account.

The experience this brings

Relationships must develop into workable business propositions, and timing must remain commercially sensible as conditions change.

Related services

  • Find and develop suitable partnerships
  • Pursue customers in other markets together
  • Develop workable agreements

Linked as transferable experience, not as a Japan–India assignment.
